QuorumAsset.note: Redeployed after adding owner() alias for issuer - required for Cleanverse's owner-signature registration checks.

factory.note: Self-serve deployment: any wallet calls deploy() and owns the result. The Quorum deployer never signs, never holds a key on it, and is provably locked out - confirmed by trying and getting NotRegisterOwner back.
factory.compiledWith: FOUNDRY_PROFILE=factory (optimizer on, size-optimised - the factory embeds all three children's creation code and exceeds EIP-170 unoptimised at the default profile's settings)

demoRegister.note: Deployed by a fresh, unrelated wallet (0x0cd1...F047) with Singapore's real parameters, not the demo's narrowed ones - proof this isn't just self-serve for the specific 5-seat pack shown elsewhere on this site.

lockoutProof.note: The Quorum deployer (0xb84b...1A06, the wallet behind every other tx on this site) called factory.issue() on this register and was refused on-chain.

seatsFilled.note: P1-P5 issued 100 QNOTE each, real transactions

p6Refused.note: P6 fully verified (SG, tier 50, personId 6) but refused on issue() - room full

walletSplit.note: P1 wallet1 -> wallet2 (30 QNOTE), wallet1 -> wallet3 (20 QNOTE). activeSeats unchanged at 5 throughout.

layer4WriteBack.note: Quorum computes the set-level answer on-chain (holdsSeat) and writes it back into each A-Pass as a subGroup tag - QS seated, QU unseated. An A-Token rule with allowed_sub_group QS then makes Cleanverse's OWN engine refuse anyone Quorum never seated, using the only rule shape their engine has: a per-wallet attribute check. The aggregate is precomputed and handed over.
layer4WriteBack.removedPermissiveRuleReason: A-Token rules are OR-combined - any matching rule allows. Verified empirically: with both a country-only rule and the QS rule present, P6 still passed on the country rule alone. The permissive rule had to be removed for the QS gate to bind.

result.significance: Person 6 is now refused twice, independently: by QuorumAsset's transfer hook, and by Cleanverse's own compliance check running their code on their infrastructure. Neither refusal depends on the other.

concentration.note: Ceiling enabled live at 3000bps (30%). P2 -> P1's SECOND wallet, 60 QNOTE: refused on-chain. The receiving wallet would have held only 12% of supply - unremarkable per-wallet - but person 1, summed across three wallets, would have crossed 30%. A 30 QNOTE transfer through the same path settled, leaving person 1 at 26%.

freezeUnfreeze.note: P3's A-Pass frozen via update_status, seat retained (activeSeats stayed 5, holdsSeat(3)=true throughout), acquisition blocked - verify_apass returned a genuine on-chain APassNotActive revert while frozen.
